pl-l4d18c2-d1e115.summary: Defines the keys as spiritual, not bodily: knowledge of discerning and power of judging, that is of binding and loosing, by which the Church's judge must admit the worthy and exclude the unworthy from the kingdom; he has the right of loosing as of binding.
claims: The keys are knowledge of discernment and power of binding and loosing.

pl-l4d18c2-d1e124.summary: Quotes Ambrose: the Lord willed the right of loosing and binding to be equal, promising both on equal terms; so one who lacks the right to loose lacks also the right to bind.
claims: The rights to bind and loose are equal and inseparable.

pl-l4d18c2-d1e133.summary: Adds Ambrose: both are permitted to the Church, heresy has neither, since this right is granted only to priests; the Church, which has true priests, rightly claims it, heresy, which lacks true priests, cannot.
claims: Only the Church's true priests have the power of the keys.

pl-l4d18c2.summary: Defines the keys as spiritual, not bodily: knowledge of discernment and power of judging, that is, of binding and loosing, by which the Church's judge admits the worthy and excludes the unworthy from the kingdom. Ambrose: the Lord gave equal right of loosing and binding, so one who lacks the right to loose lacks the right to bind; the Church has both, heresy has neither, since only true priests have it.
claims: The keys are knowledge of discernment and power of binding and loosing.
The power to bind and the power to loose go together.
Only the Church's true priests have the keys; heresy does not.
